top5.title: American voters reject data center projects
top5.description: In Alhambra, California, 83% of voters supported banning data centers, while in Wells, Maine, 82% approved a 180-day pause. OpenAI now proposes paying for electricity and infrastructure, publishing more information, and investing locally to win residents’ support.
top5.why: Voter opposition to data centers signals a growing infrastructure and permitting constraint that could raise costs and slow AI expansion.

top5.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber to research vulnerabilities
top5.description: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Cyber, a restricted model capable of finding software vulnerabilities and building exploits for authorized security testers.
top5.why: OpenAI’s launch of GPT-6 Cyber marks a significant advance in AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and raises new cybersecurity and misuse concerns.

top5.title: Employers turn against AI at work after being overwhelmed by mediocre content
top5.description: The campaign against AI-generated content in the workplace now has a powerful ally. Executives liked AI at work until they were overwhelmed by mediocre content.
top5.why: Employers’ backlash against mediocre AI-generated content could slow workplace adoption and shift demand toward higher-quality, human-supervised AI use.

top5.title: Google announces new AI controls for schools
top5.description: Google announced new school-related AI controls, raising the question of whether schools will be able to keep Search while rejecting its AI features.
top5.why: Google’s new AI controls for schools could shape how education systems balance access to productivity tools with concerns about AI governance and classroom use.

top5.title: A gut-bacteria treatment reduces infections
top5.description: In a small randomized trial, the cultured gut-bacteria treatment SER-155 reduced bloodstream infections in blood cancer patients receiving stem-cell transplants. Infections affected 10% of treated patients versus 42.9% of those receiving a placebo, but larger trials are needed.
top5.why: A gut-bacteria treatment that sharply reduced infections in high-risk transplant patients shows promising clinical potential, though larger trials are still needed.
